Subject: Operational validation & pilot scope — Fount Health (post-call)

Hi Marta — thanks again for the time today. I wanted to capture the key takeaways and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the technical deep-dive.

Quick recap of the pain you described:
- Patient triage and clinician-assist flows are sensitive to latency during peak hours (mornings 07:00–10:00 PT). Current in-house infra has p99 spikes above 1.5s which breaks UX.
- Data sensitivity: messages often contain PHI — you need an auditable, private deployment option and 12+ month retention for access logs.
- Search/knowledge retrieval: you want sentence-level embeddings for a 12M-doc corpus and sub-50ms embedding latency for batched lookups.

Model & performance requirements we discussed:
- Model family: 7B or 13B LLM (instruction-tuned) with ability to run 4-bit quantized for cost testing.
- Context window: up to 4k tokens for long consults.
- Inference SLO targets: p50 ~20–30ms per token, p95 <120ms per token, p99 <300ms for text-gen for 1–3 concurrent interactive users per session. Embeddings batch SLO: 50ms median for batches of 32.
- Availability: pilot needs 99.5% uptime SLA with predictable warm-up behavior during daily peaks.

Topology & deployment notes:
- Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) strongly preferred for PHI. We'll propose a dedicated-gpu pool in your VPC connected via private peering and a small hot-warm cache layer for prefix reuse.
- KV-cache and prefix caching expected to reduce token cost by ~30% for your workload shape (short prompts + retrieval).

Next steps (action items):
1) I’ll share a short SLO draft and a topology sketch (attached).
2) Can you confirm the peak hours and an approximate QPS during those windows? You mentioned ~120 requests/minute peak — if you can confirm that would help sizing.
3) Please confirm any compliance or procurement contacts we should loop in for SOC2 evidence and DPA redlines.
4) Proposed follow-up: technical deep-dive next Wed (Jun 30) with infra and security teams — does 10:00–11:00 PT work?

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. I’ve attached an initial SLO matrix and network notes for your review.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Vanessa — really helpful, thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak traffic: earlier estimate was rough — refined numbers: 150 requests/min peak across our two front-end services, with spikes up to ~300 requests/min during particularly high-demand events (e.g., morning digest).
- PHI: correct, we treat this as PHI; private deployment is a hard requirement for pilot. We also need 12 months for audit logs and access trails.
- Embeddings: we plan to run nightly re-embeds and expect a heavier batch job at 02:00 PT (~10k embeddings per run). For real-time UX we need <100ms for 32-item batches.

Procurement & compliance: please include our security lead (security@founthealth.com) and procurement (procure@founthealth.com) on future threads — I’ll introduce them once we have the topology + SOC2 artifacts.

Jun 30 at 10:00 PT works for the deep-dive for now — please send a calendar invite. I’ve attached the SLO matrix we use internally (slo_matrix.xlsx) that shows how we weight latency vs. correctness for each endpoint.

Thanks,
Marta
Head of Product Operations, Fount Health
Marta.Ruiz@founthealth.com
